items.section_heading: I. Solve this Nutrition Puzzle - Horizontal
items.stem: Which nutrient is the main source of energy for sport person?
items.answer: Carbohydrate. Carbohydrates are the major sources of energy for sportpersons, and their body stores of carbohydrate (glycogen) determine stamina and performance.
grounding: Carbohydrates are major sources of energy for sportpersons.
Glycogen stores determine the stamina and performance.

items.section_heading: I. Solve this Nutrition Puzzle - Horizontal
items.stem: This is one of the factors affecting meal planning.
items.answer: Age. Nutritional requirement and food choices vary with regard to age, sex, activity level and physiological condition, so age is one of the factors to be considered while planning a meal for good health and fitness. Any of the other factors the chapter lists - gender, physical activity or physiological state - answers the clue equally well; the grid that fixes the length of the word is not reproduced here.
grounding: Nutritional requirement and food choices vary with regard to their age, sex, activity level and physiological condition.
Everybody needs a balanced diet irrespective of age but certain factors influence the food choices.
Consider the following factors while planning meal for good health and fitness.

items.section_heading: I. Solve this Nutrition Puzzle - Horizontal
items.stem: The practice of adding unwanted material in food.
items.answer: Adulteration. When food quality is modified intentionally it is called food adulteration - an unhealthy and illegal practice of adding low grade ingredients to the original food or deleting the vital component, usually done intentionally to increase profits.

items.section_heading: I. Solve this Nutrition Puzzle - Horizontal
items.stem: Emissions of intense energy capable of penetrating tissues.
items.answer: Radiation. Radiations are emissions of intense energy capable of penetrating tissues; when food is exposed to a specific form of radiation (gamma rays from Cobalt 60) under controlled conditions its shelf life increases, and such food is called irradiated food.
grounding: Radiations are emissions of intense energy capable of penetrating tissues.
When food is exposed to specific form of radiation (gamma rays from Cobalt 60) under controlled conditions it increases their shelf life and is referred as irradiated food.

items.section_heading: I. Solve this Nutrition Puzzle - Vertical
items.stem: In India this authority certifies foods for safe consumption.
items.answer: FSSAI, the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India. In India it is the responsibility of FSSAI to ensure safety and quality food, and it ensures the availability of wholesome food that is safe for consumption; an FSSAI code is given to each food item.
grounding: In India it is the responsibility of Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) to ensure safety and quality food.
It ensures the availability of wholesome food that is safe for consumption.
FSSAI code is given to each food item which you can see on various food products.

items.section_heading: I. Solve this Nutrition Puzzle - Vertical
items.stem: Milk and meat help to build the body because these contain this nutrient.
items.answer: Protein. Foods like egg, whey protein, soy and milk (casein) and low fat dairy products provide good quality protein, and protein is used for building and repairing of muscles and tissues.
grounding: Foods like egg, whey protein, soy and milk (casein), low fat dairy products, grains, nuts, seeds and beans provide good quality protein.

items.section_heading: I. Solve this Nutrition Puzzle - Vertical
items.stem: Which compounds are used for food crops but can be injurious to health?
items.answer: Pesticides. Pesticides are chemicals used in agriculture to protect crops in the fields and during storage and to control insects and pests, but they often leave residues in food which are passed on to the body and can cause damage to the brain and nervous system, liver and kidneys, and are specially harmful to the fetus.
grounding: Pesticides are chemicals used in agriculture to protect crops in the fields, during storage and to control insects and pests in the surroundings, e.g., mosquitoes and cockroaches.
Pesticides often leave their residues in food which are passed on to the body.
Pesticides can cause damage to the brain and nervous system, liver, kidneys and are specially harmful to fetus.

items.stem: 'Without dietary planning it is difficult to meet the requirements of people' - discuss this statement giving suitable reasons and examples.
items.answer: Dietary planning is a process of developing meal plans for adequate nutrition within the available resources, and it is needed because nutritional requirement and food choices vary with regard to age, sex, activity level and physiological condition. One common menu therefore cannot meet everybody's requirement. For example, a healthy sedentary woman needs 1900 kcal a day while the same woman, if pregnant, will need 2200 kcal; an adult man needs 0.8 g protein per kg body weight per day, but the same person, if an athlete, requires 2.0 g protein per kg body weight per day. Adolescents grow at a fast pace and are active, so they need extra nourishment, whereas elders have difficulty in chewing, swallowing and digestion and need soft, easily digestible foods such as well cooked vegetables and idli. Planning is also a scientific method of saving energy, time and money: it makes the tasks of procuring raw material, preparing meals and ensuring food quality simpler, and it adds variety to the meals and reduces wastage. Without such planning food is chosen mostly for its taste or appearance, while nutritive value and quality go unattended and individual requirements are not met.
grounding: Dietary planning is a process of developing meal plans for adequate nutrition within the available resources.
Nutritional requirement and food choices vary with regard to their age, sex, activity level and physiological condition.
For example, a healthy sedentary woman needs 1900 kcal/day while the same woman, if pregnant, will need 2200 kcal.
Similarly an adult man needs 0.8 g protein/Kg body weight/day. The same person if an athlete requires 2.0g protein/Kg body weight/day.
Adolescents grow at a fast pace and are active, so they need extra nourishment.
Elders often have difficulty in chewing, swallowing and digestion; they need soft and easily digestible foods, such as, well cooked vegetables, idli etc.

It makes the tasks of procuring raw material, preparing meals and ensuring food quality simpler.
It adds variety the meals and reduces wastage.

items.stem: In a group there is a male teacher, a female doctor, a 15-year-old girl playing tennis and a man aged 68 years. List the factors that will be applicable for dietary planning of this group.
items.answer: The factors applicable are age, gender, physical activity, physiological state and individual food preferences, since nutritional requirement and food choices vary with regard to age, sex, activity level and physiological condition. Age: the 15-year-old is an adolescent who grows at a fast pace and is active and so needs extra nourishment, while the man aged 68 will have difficulty in chewing, swallowing and digestion and needs soft, easily digestible food. Gender: nutritional requirements vary with gender, and the female members need more iron because of blood loss during menstruation. Physical activity: the girl playing tennis needs more energy, while the teacher's and the doctor's sitting work needs less. Food preferences also vary from person to person and strongly affect the planning of meals.
grounding: Nutritional requirement and food choices vary with regard to their age, sex, activity level and physiological condition.
Adolescents grow at a fast pace and are active, so they need extra nourishment.
Elders often have difficulty in chewing, swallowing and digestion; they need soft and easily digestible foods, such as, well cooked vegetables, idli etc.
Nutritional requirements vary with gender.
Females need more iron (hemoglobin) due to blood loss during menstruation.
Energy and nutrient requirements vary with physical activity.
Sitting jobs like reading, computer work, etc., need less energy and heavy duty tasks like cycling, carrying heavy load, sports, etc., need more energy.
Food preferences vary from person to person and strongly affect planning of meals

items.stem: What kind of diet do sportspersons need? Substantiate your answer giving reasons.
items.answer: Sportspersons are constantly engaged in intense physical exercise, training, matches and competitions, so their energy and nutritional requirements are also very high, and the right kind of food given at the right time in the right proportion is of paramount importance to prolong their sporting life. Carbohydrates are their major source of energy: 3-5 g per kg body weight per day is sufficient for general fitness, while intensive sports like football, gymnastics and weight lifting may need 5-10 g per kg body weight per day, and high carbohydrate, easily digestible food 2-4 hours before training or an event gives quick energy release and replenishment. Protein requirement ranges from 1.2-2.0 g per kg body weight per day depending on the intensity of the sport, because protein is used for building and repairing of muscles and tissues. Fat is not considered a good source of energy during exercise and competition as it is metabolised very slowly, so it is better for slow, long duration events like a marathon. Vitamins and minerals are crucial because energy utilisation in the body is largely associated with them, particularly some group B vitamins and magnesium, and vitamins A, E and C prevent cell damage and act as antioxidants that improve stamina and immunity. Water and fluids are crucial to maintain the hydration level and electrolyte balance: 2-2.5 litres a day may be adequate, but up to 5-6 litres may be needed in hot weather and intense exercise. Colourful fruits and vegetables, dairy products, seeds, nuts and whole grains taken in sufficient amount supply the needed vitamins and minerals.

Depending upon the intensity of the sport, protein requirement can range from 1.2 -2.0g per kg body weight per day.

Water and fluids maintain the hydration level and electrolyte balance in the body and are crucial in sports.

items.stem: Write notes on a) Food quality b) Food preservation methods
items.answer: a) Food quality is the criteria by which a person accepts or rejects any food item, and it is crucial at every stage of food handling from farm to table. Good quality food brings health and well-being, while poor quality can cause illness and rejection of the food in the market as well. Quality is often judged in terms of microbiological load and alterations in the physical parameters and chemical composition of food; physical examination is done on the basis of size, shape, colour, texture and visual appeal, and the food should be free from dirt, cracks or foreign material, from contamination by bacteria, mould, virus and yeast, and from infestation by insects and pests. Quality marks like FSSAI, AGMARK and ISI should be observed while selecting food. Food quality is favourably altered by techniques of food preservation, and nutritional quality can be enhanced by fortification. b) Food preservation is the process of treating and handling food to stop or slow down spoilage and extend the shelf life of food; it works on the principles of reducing the moisture content, preventing the growth of micro-organisms causing spoilage and controlling enzymatic activity. Its methods are heat treatment, where heat destroys the harmful microorganisms, as in pasteurisation of milk and sterilisation of bottles; refrigeration and freezing, where low temperature limits enzymatic and microbial activities; drying or dehydration, which removes the moisture without which microbes cannot grow; addition of natural or chemical preservatives, such as sugar in jams and jellies, salt, spices and oil in pickles, and sodium benzoate or potassium meta bisulphite (KMS) in ketchups and squashes; and preservation by radiation, in which food exposed to gamma rays from Cobalt 60 under controlled conditions becomes irradiated food of longer shelf life.
grounding: Food quality is the criteria by which a person accepts or rejects any food item.
It is crucial at every stage of food handling from farm to table.
Good quality food brings health and well-being and poor quality can cause illness and rejection of food in the market as well.
Quality of food is often judged in terms of microbiological load and alterations in physical parameters and chemical composition of food.
Physical examination of food is done on the basis of size, shape, color, texture and visual appeal.
It is necessary to observe the quality marks, like FSSAI, AGMARK and ISI, on the food articles while selection to ensure quality.
Food quality is favorably altered by techniques of food preservation. It is also possible to enhance nutritional quality of food by fortification.
Food preservation is the process of treating and handling food to stop or slow down spoilage and extend shelf life of food.
It works on the principles of reducing the moisture content, preventing the growth of micro organisms causing spoilage and controlling enzymatic activity.
Heat treatment: Application of heat helps in preserving food by destroying the harmful microorganisms.
For example, Pasteurisation of milk and sterilisation of bottles.
Refrigeration and freezing: Low temperature limit the enzymatic and microbial activities keeping the food safe for longer duration.
Drying or dehydration: This technique is based on reducing or removing the moisture content of food as microbes cannot grow in the absence of water.
Addition of preservatives: Preservatives are natural or chemical ingredients which selectively control the growth of microorganisms and enzymes in food and restrict spoilage.
Jams and jellies are preserved by sugar and pickles by salt, spices and oil.
Chemical preservatives like sodium benzoate or Potassium Meta bisulphite (KMS) are used in ketchups and squashes.
When food is exposed to specific form of radiation (gamma rays from Cobalt 60) under controlled conditions it increases their shelf life and is referred as irradiated food.

items.stem: 'Even the most nutritious food may not be safe to eat if adulterated' discuss the statement giving cases/examples in the light of what you know about food adulteration?
items.answer: Nutritious food too, if contaminated or adulterated, is not safe for consumption, as it may cause infection or disease. Food adulteration is an unhealthy and illegal practice of adding low grade ingredients to the original food or deleting the vital component, usually done intentionally to increase profits; it makes the food unsafe to eat, degrades the food quality and is injurious to health. Many a time the food is adulterated in such a way that it looks the same, but soon it may change in taste, appearance and nutritional composition. Cases from the chapter show how ordinary nutritious foods are affected: milk adulterated with water flows immediately down a polished surface without leaving a mark, and milk adulterated with starch turns blue when 2-3 drops of tincture iodine are added; red chilli powder adulterated with Rodamine gives an immediate red colour with acetone; arhar dal adulterated with metanil yellow gives a pink colour with lukewarm water and a few drops of HCl; and papaya seeds mixed in black pepper float on water while pure pepper settles. Consuming such food can cause diarrhoea, vomiting, headache, abdominal cramps and fatigue; sometimes the impact is not instantly visible but distorts the functioning of the immune, digestive and nervous system, and it can also lead to liver disorder, heart disease, paralysis, brain damage and cancer. Adulterated food eaten by pregnant women may lead to abortion or damage the brain of the baby, and children, pregnant and lactating women, elderly people and weak or sick persons are at higher risk. Hence nutritive value alone does not make a food safe.
grounding: Nutritious food too, if contaminated or adulterated is not safe for consumption as it may cause infection or disease.

items.stem: Suggest a method to detect: a) Metanil yellow adulteration in arhar dal b) Papaya seeds adulteration in peppercorns
items.answer: a) Metanil yellow in arhar dal: extract the colour from the sample of the pulse with lukewarm water and add a few drops of HCl; a pink colour indicates the presence of metanil yellow. b) Papaya seeds in peppercorns: put the sample in water - pure black pepper settles at the bottom, whereas papaya seeds float on the surface of the water.

items.stem: What are the various ways of protection from harmful effects of pesticides?
items.answer: The chapter's preventive measures are: use herbal or bio-pesticides; use organic food; wash fruits and vegetables thoroughly under clean running water; keep the pesticides in locked cabinets, away from the kitchen and bathroom; and read all labels and warnings carefully before using pesticides. Young children, pregnant and lactating women and weak and sick persons are at higher risk and hence should be specially protected. Also, if pesticide is used in accordance with good agricultural practice the residual level would be low and consumption of such foods will not be harmful.

Wash fruits and vegetables thoroughly under clean running water.
Use organic food.

items.stem: Which of the following is food adulteration?

options.label: B
options.text: Abstraction of a constituent of food article

options.label: D
options.text: Splitting of a food article in small pieces

items.answer: B. The chapter's criteria designating a food as adulterated include the abstraction, wholly or in part, of any of its constituents, which is the same thing as deleting the vital component from the original food; a preservative or a food colour is adulteration only if it is not the one specified or is more than the prescribed quantity, and splitting a food article into small pieces does not alter its composition at all.
grounding: There is abstraction, wholly or in part, of any of its constituents.
deleting the vital component. It is usually done intentionally to increase the profits.
There is presence of any coloring matter or preservatives other than that specified in respect thereof or in quantity more than prescribed.

items.stem: Match the following a) Turmeric (i) Caution b) Microbial load (ii) Anti inflammatory c) Pesticides (iii) Shelf life d) Semi-perishable (iv) Food Quality
items.answer: a-(ii), b-(iv), c-(i), d-(iii). Microbial load goes with food quality, because the quality of food is often judged in terms of microbiological load and alterations in physical parameters and chemical composition. Pesticides go with caution, because pesticides are toxic in nature, their labels and warnings must be read before use and they must be kept in locked cabinets away from the kitchen. Semi-perishable goes with shelf life, because foods are classified by shelf life and a semi-perishable food remains fresh and edible for about a week (5-7 days). Turmeric is therefore left with anti inflammatory; note that the chapter itself names turmeric only as a commonly adulterated food and does not state its anti-inflammatory property, so that one pair follows from elimination and not from the chapter.
grounding: Quality of food is often judged in terms of microbiological load and alterations in physical parameters and chemical composition of food.
Those at higher risks are workers handling or producing pesticides as pesticides are toxic in nature.
Read all labels and warnings carefully before using pesticides.
The duration of time during which the food item remains fit for consumption at room temperature is called shelf life which determines perishability.
Semi-perishable which remain fresh and edible for about a week (5-7 days) e.g., some vegetables and fruits.
Natural turmeric powder leaves a light yellow colour while settling down whereas adulterated turmeric powder will leave a strong yellow colour in water.

items.stem: Discuss the classification of food based on shelf life. Take an example of a semi-perishable food and explain various methods of increasing its shelf life.
items.answer: The duration of time during which a food item remains fit for consumption at room temperature is called its shelf life, and it determines perishability. On this basis foods are of three kinds: perishable foods, which remain fresh and edible for a few hours to 1-2 days only, for example milk, meat and green leafy vegetables; semi-perishable foods, which remain fresh and edible for about a week (5-7 days), for example some vegetables and fruits; and non-perishable foods, which remain fresh and edible for more than a month, for example grains, sugar, oil and pulses. Knowledge of the approximate shelf life of different foods helps in reducing spoilage, and proper storage of food decreases food spoilage. Taking fruit, a semi-perishable food, as the example, its shelf life can be increased by refrigeration and freezing, because low temperature limits the enzymatic and microbial activities and keeps the food safe for a longer duration; by drying or dehydration, which removes the moisture content, as microbes cannot grow in the absence of water; by heat treatment, which destroys the harmful microorganisms; by the addition of preservatives, as jams and jellies made from fruit are preserved by sugar and squashes by chemical preservatives like sodium benzoate or potassium meta bisulphite (KMS); and by irradiation, since fruits exposed to gamma rays from Cobalt 60 under controlled conditions have an increased shelf life.

Semi-perishable which remain fresh and edible for about a week (5-7 days) e.g., some vegetables and fruits.
Non-perishable which remain fresh and edible for more than a month, e.g., grains, sugar, oil, pulses.

Proper storage of food decreases food spoilage
Refrigeration and freezing: Low temperature limit the enzymatic and microbial activities keeping the food safe for longer duration.
Drying or dehydration: This technique is based on reducing or removing the moisture content of food as microbes cannot grow in the absence of water.
Heat treatment: Application of heat helps in preserving food by destroying the harmful microorganisms.
Jams and jellies are preserved by sugar and pickles by salt, spices and oil.
Chemical preservatives like sodium benzoate or Potassium Meta bisulphite (KMS) are used in ketchups and squashes.
Items like fruits, potatoes, onions, spices, herbs and some ready-to-eat foods can be preserved in this way.
